objectives: State the structure of a design system.
Apply design tokens for theming + accessibility.

slides.title: Design systems: why + what
slides.body:
**Design system**: codified library of components + patterns + guidelines + tokens used across products.

Without a design system: each designer/team picks their own colors, type, components → inconsistent UX, duplicated work, accessibility gaps.

With a design system: shared source of truth. Same Button component used in all products; updating once propagates. Designers + devs reference the same elements.

**Major design systems**:
- **Material Design** (Google): Android default; widely adopted.
- **Apple HIG (Human Interface Guidelines)**: iOS / macOS standard.
- **Microsoft Fluent**: Windows + Microsoft 365.
- **IBM Carbon**: open-source, enterprise.
- **Atlassian Design System**: Jira, Confluence.
- **Salesforce Lightning**: large CRM ecosystem.
- **GitHub Primer**: GitHub.com.
- **Shopify Polaris**: e-commerce admin.
- **Adobe Spectrum**: Adobe products.

Each codifies thousands of decisions about typography, color, spacing, components, motion, content tone, accessibility.

**Components of a design system**:
- **Foundations / tokens**: colors, type, spacing, radii, shadows, motion durations.
- **Components**: Button, Card, Modal, Form, Navigation, etc.
- **Patterns**: how components combine. Modal-confirmation, form-validation patterns.
- **Guidelines**: voice + tone, content writing, accessibility rules.
- **Documentation**: usage examples, do's + don'ts.

**Storybook** (popular open-source tool): runs your component library as an interactive catalog. Developers + designers see the same source. Used by GitHub, Lyft, Adobe, etc.

slides.title: Design tokens
Atomic design + the design-system organization
slides.body:
**Atomic Design** (Brad Frost 2013): organize components into hierarchical levels.

- **Atoms**: smallest units. Button, Input, Label, Icon.
- **Molecules**: combinations of atoms. SearchField = Input + Button. Form Field = Label + Input + ErrorMessage.
- **Organisms**: more complex combinations. Header = Logo + Navigation + UserMenu. Card = Image + Title + Body + Button.
- **Templates**: page-level layouts (without content).
- **Pages**: templates with real content.

Nomenclature is sometimes contested (alternatives: components/patterns/templates). The principle: BUILD UP from small reusable pieces.

**Design-system team structure**:
- **Federation**: small core team + contributors from product teams. Most common.
- **Centralized**: dedicated team owns + updates. Quality high; pace slower.
- **Decentralized**: each team builds own. Fragmented; not really a design system.

**Adoption challenges**:
- **Convincing teams**: 'we're special / fast / different' resistance.
- **Customization needs**: not every product fits the system perfectly.
- **Versioning**: when system updates, products may break.
- **Documentation debt**: docs lag implementation.

**Governance**:
- **Contribution model**: how teams propose changes. Often PR-style.
- **Review process**: maintainer reviews; design + dev + accessibility check.
- **Release cadence**: regular updates with semver.
- **Deprecation**: how to retire patterns gracefully.

**Modern + emerging**:
- **Headless components** (Radix, Headless UI): unstyled accessible primitives. Each product adds its own styles. Removes styling debate from the system.
- **shadcn/ui**: copy-paste components rather than NPM dependency. Each project owns + customizes.
- **AI-generated components**: vibrant area. Galileo AI, Uizard, v0 generate UI from text prompts. Used for early ideation; refined by humans for production.

question.question: Design a token-based color system
question.goal: Design system supports both light + dark mode. Define semantic tokens that work in both.

steps.prompt: Primitive layer: define color scales. Example: gray-50, gray-100, ..., gray-900 (light to dark). What about for primary brand?

options: Each brand color has its scale: primary-50, primary-100, ..., primary-900 (light to dark blue, say). Same for semantic colors (success, warning, error).

steps.reveal: Scales (50-900) for each color: neutral, primary, success, warning, error. ~50-100 primitives.

steps.prompt: Semantic layer: 'color-text-primary'. Light theme = gray-900 (dark text on light bg). Dark theme value?

options: gray-50 (light text on dark bg) — semantic stays the same name, primitive mapping reverses for dark.

steps.reveal: Dark theme: color-text-primary = gray-50 (light gray). The SEMANTIC token's name is theme-agnostic; the underlying primitive flips.

steps.prompt: Critical: ensure contrast in BOTH themes. e.g., color-text-primary on color-bg-surface ≥ 4.5:1. How verify?

options: Tooling: tokens-studio-Figma plugin, Stark for design, automated tests in code. Compute contrast ratios across all combinations + flag any below WCAG threshold.

steps.reveal: Automate contrast checks across all combinations. Both themes. Modern systems include this as a CI test on token changes. Prevents accidental accessibility regressions.

question.finalResult: $$\boxed{\text{Tokens: primitives → semantic → component, theme-swap at semantic layer}}$$ Design tokens make multi-theme + multi-brand systems tractable. Without tokens, themes require touching every component. With tokens, themes are a single primitive-mapping file swap. Modern tools (Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, the W3C tokens spec) standardize the workflow. Accessibility enforcement at the token layer prevents regressions.

question.question: Your company has 10 product teams + introduces a design system. Six months in, only 2 teams have adopted it. What's typical + how to improve?
options: Common: adoption is slow because: (1) teams have custom needs; (2) migration takes time; (3) docs may be unclear. Improve by: dedicated migration help; documenting use-cases; sponsorship from leadership; making opt-out painful (org-wide design reviews flag non-compliant designs).
question.explanation: Design-system adoption is THE hardest part. Common reasons for slow adoption: customization needs, migration cost, unclear docs, lack of leadership backing, change-aversion. Fixes: dedicated migration help (a 'design system team' that goes to product teams + helps them migrate), prominent docs + examples, executive sponsorship ('every new feature uses the system'), social pressure (design reviews flag non-compliant designs). Most mature systems take 2-3 years to reach high adoption.

slides.workedSolution: Adoption is slow because: teams busy with features, customization needs, learning curve, governance friction. Fixes: pair each product team with a system contributor; document examples; leadership backing; phase-in (new code = system; gradual migrate). Major systems (Material, Polaris, Carbon) took years to reach >90% adoption across products.

question.question: Design system has 80 color primitives + 30 semantic + 50 component tokens. Total tokens (for a single theme)?
Multi-brand design system
question.prompt: Your company acquires 3 smaller brands + wants to unify on one design system while keeping distinct brand identities. Walk through the token + component strategy.
Explain in two or three sentences why design tokens have become foundational to modern design systems.
question.rubric: Mentions that tokens decouple design decisions (semantic intent) from raw values; enable themes (light/dark) + brands + accessibility constraints by swapping primitive mappings; provide a contract between designers + developers (both reference the same names); without tokens, multi-theme + multi-brand systems are impractical.
